headline: South African startup Vambo AI has released MORENA, a small open-weight AI model built from scratch for 12 African languages, but has not yet published evidence for its performance claims.
score_reason: Kept at pool 5: a real release for under-served languages, but the performance claim is unverified and the licence is unknown.
importance_line: Developers and researchers working in African languages could get a cheaper base model to build on, but the performance claim is the founder's own, and no results, licence or download details are published.
summary: iAfrica reports that Vambo AI, a South African startup, has released MORENA, an open-weight model (its trained settings are public) with 1.5 billion parameters (a measure of model size), trained from scratch for 12 African languages plus English and French, and that co-founder Isheanesu Misi says it handles African-language text better than a Google model eight times larger. iAfrica points out that the claim names no test, no Google model and no results, and that licence and download details are missing.
notes: Read iAfrica in full. Release date not stated in the article.
